reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific mechanistic claims about diffusion, phase separation, and brittle precipitate formation under mechanical loading, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific coupling of high strain-rate loading with enhanced diffusion and phase separation in high-entropy alloys, so citations are required.
premises: Mechanical loading induces local stress concentrations and enhanced diffusion that trigger compositional fluctuations
Compositional fluctuations lead to nucleation of secondary brittle phases
Brittle precipitates act as crack nucleation sites
Phase separation and precipitate formation occur under high strain-rate or cyclic loading at moderate elevated temperatures
The process leads to a measurable loss of toughness relative to the as-cast state
